clue.text: Short measure given while in main shopping area

indicators.note: in tells us one word is placed inside the other, the period word going into the shopping-area word

parts.note: a town's centre is its main shopping district
a while is a stretch of time

explanation.surface: A brief size is quoted for something in the high street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' is only a link; 'while' looks like a conjunction but is the noun meaning a period.
explanation.definitionFit: A hundredth of a metre is a small unit of length.

clue.text: Female adviser, for instance, up-river

parts.note: eg abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the river's name is read upwards, back to front

parts.note: the Aire is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A woman counsellor is placed, say, further up a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upriver' splits into 'up' (reverse) and 'river' (AIRE, a Yorkshire river).
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman legend this nymph counselled King Numa, and her name came to mean a woman mentor.

clue.text: Son not making strenuous efforts in schooling

indicators.note: not says the son letter is left out of the effort word

parts.note: straining is exerting oneself hard

explanation.surface: A boy does not overexert himself during lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: Instruction or coaching in a skill is education.

clue.text: Document raised problem about an underground vault, say

indicators.note: about means the reversed problem word goes around the little word an
raised in a down clue means the word is read upwards

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem

indicators.note: say means we want what sounds like the vault word, not its spelling

parts.note: a crypt is an underground chamber beneath a church

explanation.surface: A paper raises an issue about a burial chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns the sum upwards, as a down clue is read; 'say' signals a sound-alike, so the vault word is spelt as it is pronounced, not as written.
explanation.definitionFit: A handwritten text or an author's original copy is a written document.

clue.text: Crime of army lad encompassing overthrow of sovereign

indicators.note: encompassing says the army and lad pieces wrap round the overturned ruler

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

indicators.note: overthrow turns the sovereign upside down, which in a down clue reverses the letters

parts.note: ER is the royal cipher, Elizabeth Regina
a son is a lad

explanation.surface: A young soldier is charged with plotting to topple the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overthrow' turns the royal cipher upside down, which in a down clue reverses it; 'encompassing' puts it inside the army abbreviation before the lad.
explanation.definitionFit: Betraying one's country or plotting against its ruler is the gravest offence against the state.

clue.text: Dame Rebecca's bridge partner?

parts.note: the writer Dame Rebecca West shares her surname with a bridge seat, and the player opposite that seat is the partner

explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North partners South and the other two seats partner each other.
explanation.definitionFit: The compass point opposite West is the partner seat at the bridge table.

clue.text: Woman in charge in the gentlemen's home

indicators.note: the second in places the charge abbreviation inside the city

parts.note: Shakespeare's Two Gentlemen of Verona come from that Italian city
IC is the standard abbreviation for in charge, as in a person IC of a unit

explanation.surface: A lady runs the household at a gentlemen's residence.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' belongs to 'in charge' (IC); the second is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, borne for instance by the saint who wiped Christ's face.

clue.text: Broadcast concert has extremely unusual means of entry

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert

indicators.note: extremely takes the outer letters of the word unusual

parts.note: a gate is a way in

explanation.surface: A concert has an odd door arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To make an idea or law widely known is to proclaim or spread it.

clue.text: Seem to change sides at end of judicial review

indicators.note: changing sides swaps left for right, and at end of says the swap happens in the final letter

parts.note: an appeal asks a higher court to review a judgment

explanation.surface: Lawyers are told to switch allegiance once a court case is reconsidered.
explanation.walkthrough: Sides are L (left) and R (right): the closing L of APPEAL becomes R.
explanation.definitionFit: To come across as something is to look or give the impression of it.

clue.text: Prisoner of French army — one born in France

parts.note: de is French for of
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
I is the Roman numeral one
née is French for born, used before a maiden name

explanation.surface: A captive of the French forces turns out to be a native of France.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone held in custody is a captive.

clue.text: No meat or stew? It may be reserved for the waiters

definitions.text: It may be reserved for the waiters

indicators.note: to stew is to cook ingredients together until they break down, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A diner without meat or casserole is shown to a private room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stew' reads as a dish but tells you to rearrange NO MEAT OR; the waiters are people waiting, not restaurant staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A small room outside a main chamber is where visitors wait to be admitted.

clue.text: Periodical originally intended for sorcerers

parts.note: a magazine, informally a mag, is a periodical

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word intended

explanation.surface: A magazine at first meant for wizards.
explanation.definitionFit: The wise men of the Nativity were Persian priests, a class associated with magic.

clue.text: He grumbles when no seafood is served up with Spanish wine

indicators.note: served up in a down clue means the no-seafood pair is read upwards

parts.note: taken as written
a clam is a shellfish
tent is an old name for a dark red Spanish wine

explanation.surface: A diner complains when there is no shellfish to go with the wine.
explanation.walkthrough: TENT is a rich red wine from Spain, mainly a crossword word now.
explanation.definitionFit: A discontented person who complains constantly is a grumbler.

clue.text: Dramatic commentators discover female singer and dancer

parts.note: in Greek drama the chorus comments on the action
a girl is a female

explanation.surface: Theatre critics find a woman who can both sing and dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discover' is a link meaning the first piece finds the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a stage line-up performs songs and dance routines in a revue.

clue.text: Girl stopped supporting the races, being on her own

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue means the stopped word sits below the races

parts.note: Una is a girl's name
the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle races on the Isle of Man
ended means stopped

explanation.surface: A woman gave up backing horses and was left alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a link; the TT races are the Isle of Man motorbike races.
explanation.definitionFit: Left alone with no one watching or accompanying is solitary.

clue.text: Apathetic archbishop I'd seen around University

indicators.note: seen around means the archbishop and I'd together wrap round the university letter

parts.note: Cosmo Lang was Archbishop of Canterbury in the 1930s
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A listless senior cleric says he spotted himself near a college.
explanation.walkthrough: You need to know Cosmo Lang, Archbishop of Canterbury from 1928 to 1942.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone listless and lacking energy is without enthusiasm.

clue.text: Bird which keeps an Athenian character from church

parts.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
that serves as the relative pronoun which

explanation.surface: A bird stops a Greek from going to church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps ... from' is the surface's picture of the pronoun standing between the Greek letter and the church, keeping them apart, which fixes the order.
explanation.definitionFit: A small tree-climbing songbird that cracks nuts is a woodland species.

clue.text: Accountants almost rescue a plant

parts.note: CAs are chartered accountants

indicators.note: almost means the word for rescue loses its final letter

parts.note: to rescue is to save

explanation.surface: The bookkeepers nearly bail out a struggling business.
explanation.definitionFit: Manioc is a tropical shrub grown for its starchy root.

clue.text: It shows us the way to authenticate letters

parts.note: to sign a document is to authenticate it
the post is letters delivered

explanation.surface: Guidance is offered on how to validate correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside pointer tells travellers which direction to take.

clue.text: Come safely through the damage surrounding it

indicators.note: surrounding says the damage word wraps round the word the

parts.note: wear is damage from use

explanation.surface: Surviving the havoc that surrounds it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' points back to 'the', the word that WEAR surrounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride out a storm or crisis is to survive it.

clue.text: At the hospital he's old-fashioned and uncomplaining

parts.note: something out is no longer in fashion
a patient person bears things without complaint

explanation.surface: A hospital visitor is described as behind the times but long-suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the phrase 'he's at the hospital', describing someone attending for treatment without staying.
explanation.definitionFit: A person treated at a clinic without being admitted overnight attends the hospital.

clue.text: Strong wind a Highland Scot reported

indicators.note: reported tells us the word is as heard spoken, not as written

parts.note: a Gael is a Gaelic-speaking Highlander

explanation.surface: A Scottish Highlander tells of a fierce storm.
explanation.definitionFit: A very strong blow of air ranks high on the Beaufort scale.

clue.text: Article carried in ship is long and very narrow

indicators.note: carried in says the article goes inside the ship

parts.note: a liner is a passenger ship
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Something carried aboard a vessel is long and slim.
explanation.definitionFit: Something resembling a line is elongated and thin.

clue.text: Send conveyance that holds a large number

indicators.note: holds says the conveyance word contains the number

parts.note: transit is the conveying of people or goods
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A vehicle is dispatched carrying a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass on or broadcast a signal is to convey it.

clue.text: Insect an old woman unhesitatingly identifies

indicators.note: unhesitatingly drops the hesitation sound er from the word

parts.note: old woman is slang for one's mother

explanation.surface: An elderly lady recognises a bug without pausing.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the written form of a hesitation, so MOTHER without it is MOTH.
explanation.definitionFit: A nocturnal winged creature related to the butterfly.

clue.text: The lightest stuff in the world, symbolized in the Aldwych finale

definitions.text: The lightest stuff in the world, symbolized in the Aldwych finale

parts.words: The lightest stuff in the world, symbolized in the Aldwych finale
parts.note: the lightest element has the chemical symbol H, which is also the last letter of Aldwych

explanation.surface: A London theatre's closing show is said to be the lightest entertainment going.
explanation.walkthrough: The Aldwych is a London street and theatre known for farces; its finale is just its final letter, H.
explanation.definitionFit: The first element of the periodic table is the least dense gas.

clue.text: Most enjoyable confections featured in certain books

indicators.note: featured in means the sweets go inside the books

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a particular set of books
ices are frozen confections

explanation.surface: The tastiest sweets appear in particular volumes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasantest is the superlative of agreeable.

clue.text: Traditional yet hardier materials

indicators.note: materials are raw stuff to be made into something, so these letters are worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: Old-style fabrics that are nevertheless tougher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'materials' looks like a noun of the surface but tells you to rearrange YET HARDIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something handed down the generations is passed on by custom or inheritance.
